name: NOAA H11983 original 1–4 m variable-resolution MLLW BAG near Point St. George

producer.name: NOAA National Ocean Service, Office of Coast Survey

spatial.horizontal_crs: Original BAG compound CRS; see native audit metadata

temporal.update_cadence: Historical 2008 survey; monthly source and chart review

evidence.supports: Original survey identity, 2008 dates, report and variable-resolution BAG link.
Original report Appendix I lists eleven historical dangers, including seven underwater rocks; three starred rocks lack a known least depth. It says no bottom samples were assigned.

Original e8882503208671ca5efea41bb191027ae31293faecacb3770f7b1d3eb7e65d24 BAG opened: 10,088 native grids at 1–4 m and 35,591,242 source-cell associations passing the nominal 25–200 ft MLLW/uncertainty planning screen; see dist/data/noaa-h11983-native-source-review.json.

provenance.access_service: NOAA NCEI original BAG; USGS 2009 c109nc camera archive
transformations: Opened the original SHA-256-pinned variable-resolution BAG, inspected embedded MLLW and product uncertainty and screened every native <=4 m refinement cell.
Checked complete native supergrid footprints against a dated 155-feature CDFW MPA snapshot.
Cross-compared one NOAA NBS tile and the original BAG at 2009 camera observations; only three historical rocky windows passed both 25 m native-cell screens.
Compared those three private camera locations with 11 original report dangers and 18 bounded NOAA ENC Direct danger layers; published only aggregate distances.

limitations: The rectangular raster envelope is not continuous measured coverage; native refinement cell masks, depth and uncertainty must be checked for each proposed site.
The three original-grid-qualified historical rocky camera windows are correlated 2009 observations, not three independent reefs, current fish locations or mapped rock footprints.
The 2008 report includes eleven dangers and three rocks without known least depth. The bounded ENC proximity check is not a certified present chart, complete route or safe access review.

MPA geometry is a dated snapshot, and federal-area rules, species/date/method restrictions, source rights and habitat footprint require separate review. No fishing target, score or export is approved.
